relations.label: anticipates
relations.reason: Proposes the dual of the entire Standard Model, one dual field per field, as the dark matter sector: a conference restatement of Minic 2020. What 'dual' means differs from the program. Here it is the metastring's dual sector, the x̃ half of a doubled, T-duality-covariant, phase-space-like geometry with non-commutativity parameter λ, and the choice of spacetime is ambiguous up to T-duality. In the program it is the other Lagrangian polarization of one phase space at ℏ (#11 P2′, P5). The coupling also differs: the dual sector is 'correlated/entangled' with visible matter and detectable through it, while #11 P4 strict allows gravity only.

relations.label: related
relations.reason: Dark energy is the curvature of the dual spacetime. Nothing in the paper has a dual sector collapsing or contracting.

items.summary: This is the school's clearest conference-proceedings statement of C1's core. It proposes a dual Standard Model as the dark matter sector. That sector is correlated with visible matter, which bears on the record's 'correlated' clause, and it offers a conditional explanation of direct-detection null results. Dark energy is the curvature of the dual spacetime. Its dual is the metastring's x̃, not the conjugate polarization at ℏ. It says nothing about a velocity-gated self-interaction or about monopoles.

items.summary: In conference terms, the record's first statement of C1's core (Minic 2020, posted 2020-02-29) is the write-up of an invited talk. It was given at MPHYS10 on 9 September 2019, about 5½ months before the arXiv posting, and at the PTRel conference, a Bangkok workshop, Penn State IGC's Multimessenger Universe conference, the Miami winter conference and a Granada meeting on quantum-gravity phenomenology, none of them dated in the paper. The earliest written statement still dates from 29 February 2020. An oral presentation on the topic is documented, by title only, from 9 September 2019.

overall:
I swept conference abstracts, slides and proceedings from 2015 to 2026: 90 full-text queries on CERN Indico (113 contributions and 3,288 attachment files screened), 75 contribution dumps and INSPIRE proceedings sets totalling 19,740 records (TeVPA, ICHEP, IDM, PATRAS, DSU, Planck, PASCOS, SUSY, Lepton-Photon, Marcel Grossmann, Invisibles25), one book of abstracts and seven programme pages.

The record's three clauses, in conference form:
- **Core published.** Confirmed. The only conference statements of dark matter as the dual counterpart of visible matter come from the school. Edmonds, Minić and Takeuchi at MG16 (July 2021; arXiv 2021-09-27): "Thus the entire SM would have a dual SM (which we propose, describes the dark matter sector)." The dual there is the metastring's x̃ sector, at the string scale λ, not the conjugate polarization at ℏ.
- **Correlated.** Confirmed in the same text. The dual sector is "correlated to the visible sector via the dark energy sector", and dark matter is "detectable through ... correlation/entanglement to visible matter", where #11 P4 strict allows gravity only.
- **Neither form.** Confirmed for conference venues. No abstract or slide pairs conjugate or dual matter with a self-interaction gated by relative velocity or by momentum overlap, and none places monopoles in momentum space. The closest items: standard velocity-dependent self-interacting dark matter; an excited-dark-matter velocity "gate" (UK-APP 2026, after Finkbeiner and Weiner 2007), which opens above a threshold, the reverse of the program's knee; and hidden-sector monopole dark matter in ordinary position space (Terning and Verhaaren 2019, Ho and Takahashi 2019, Bagherian et al. 2026).

One nuance for the record, which dates the first statement to the arXiv posting of Minic 2020 (29 February 2020). That paper is the write-up of a talk ("In this talk I review recent work"). The MPHYS10 timetable puts the talk, "From string theory and quantum gravity to dark matter and dark energy", on 9 September 2019, and the acknowledgement names five more venues. The 2019 content is documented by its title only (no slides found), so the first written statement stays 29 February 2020, but an oral presentation on the topic is documented about 5½ months earlier. The school's earlier conference talks on dark matter (Pheno 2012, title only; MG14 2015; DSU 2018; Ng 2025) concern dark matter correlated with baryons and Λ, without the dual identification. Leigh's 2015 talk states that taking space-time as the target breaks Born reciprocity (already credited in #11 §3), with no dark matter.

The other conjectures:
- **C4.** Winn's 2025 abstract (SUSY 2025 talk 20 August, Lepton-Photon 2025 25 August, Invisibles25 1–5 September) gives every SM particle a magnetically charged dual that shares our photon, hidden in neutral composites. That is the shared-photon form without the momentum placement (partial; another agent is verifying it).
- **Evidence against the position-space versions of the monopole ideas.** The Parker-type bound on milli-magnetic monopole dark matter (Graesser 2023), and "No room for monopole dark matter" in the minimal model (2026 talks, apparently flag 68's paper). Neither tests p-localization.
- **C2.** "Monopoles in momentum space" at conferences means Berry-curvature (Weyl) monopoles, a collision.
- **C3.** Only competing explanations of the null result: inflation, enhanced annihilation, Winn's confinement.
- **C5.** Only related items: CPT-mirror universes, Popławski's universe in a black hole, the school's dark energy as the curvature of the dual spacetime.
- **C6, C7.** Nothing beyond standard self-interacting dark matter, long-range dark-matter forces and condensate talks.

Other collisions to know for future searches: "magnetic mirror" (plasma traps), "self-conjugate dark matter" (charge conjugation), and "dual matter" meaning monopoles in N=2 SQED. A pre-2015 lead outside the window: the Maximal Mass Model (Mateev, Primorsko 2010) proposes dark-matter candidates from anti-de Sitter momentum-space geometry, without an ordinary analogue, coupled by gravitation and Higgs exchange. It is related to C1, not a statement of it.
